concepts.title: Sound is a longitudinal wave that needs a medium
concepts.body: Sound is a type of mechanical wave that travels through a medium by compressing and rarefying particles. It cannot travel in a vacuum because there are no particles to vibrate. For example, you cannot hear a ringing bell in outer space because there is no air to carry the sound.

concepts.title: Frequency, wavelength, amplitude, pitch, and loudness
concepts.body: Frequency is the number of vibrations per second, measured in Hertz (Hz). Wavelength is the distance between two consecutive compressions or rarefactions. Amplitude is the maximum displacement of particles from their mean position. Pitch is determined by frequency, while loudness depends on amplitude. For example, a high-pitched whistle has a higher frequency than a low-pitched drum.

concepts.title: Reflection of sound and echo
concepts.body: When sound waves hit a hard surface, they bounce back, a phenomenon called reflection. If the reflected sound is heard distinctly after the original sound, it is called an echo. For example, shouting in a large empty hall produces an echo due to sound reflection.

formulas.title: Wave speed v = f x lambda
formulas.body: Wave speed (v in m/s) equals frequency (f in Hz) multiplied by wavelength (lambda in m). This formula is used to calculate the speed of sound in a medium.

formulas.title: Echo distance d = v x t / 2
formulas.body: Echo distance (d in m) equals wave speed (v in m/s) multiplied by time (t in s) divided by 2. This formula is used to calculate the distance of an object causing an echo.

examples.title: Everyday example
examples.body: When you speak, your vocal cords vibrate, creating sound waves that travel through the air to reach the listener's ears. The cause is the vibration of vocal cords.

examples.title: Applied example
examples.body: Sonar technology uses sound waves to detect underwater objects. The sound waves reflect off the object and return to the sonar device, calculating the distance. The cause is the reflection of sound waves.

mcqs.question: What type of wave is sound?
mcqs.explanation: Sound is a longitudinal wave because particles vibrate parallel to the direction of wave propagation. Transverse waves vibrate perpendicularly, electromagnetic waves do not need a medium, and mechanical waves include both longitudinal and transverse waves.

mcqs.question: A sound wave has a frequency of 500 Hz and a wavelength of 0.68 m. What is its speed?
mcqs.explanation: Using v = f x lambda, v = 500 Hz x 0.68 m = 340 m/s. The other options are incorrect because they do not match the calculated value.

mcqs.question: A person hears an echo after 2 seconds. If the speed of sound is 340 m/s, what is the distance to the reflecting surface?
mcqs.explanation: Using d = v x t / 2, d = 340 m/s x 2 s / 2 = 340 m / 2 = 170 m. The other options are incorrect because they do not account for the division by 2.
